thread:
alex: Quick heads-up — perf regression after merging fused-QKV+epilogue patch (PR #482). Microbench shows big latency bump for long sequences: baseline vs new. Anyone seen this pattern before?

priya: Yikes. Can you paste the exact bench command + model config? Also which FlashAttention variant did you compare against?

alex: Bench command I used: `./run_attention_bench --model=gpt2xl --seq=2048 --bsz=1 --kernel=fused_qkv_epilogue`
Here are the quick numbers I collected (p50, single GPU):
```
seq  bsz  kernel                 p50_ms
512   1   flash_v1               11.2
512   1   fused_qkv              10.8
2048  1   flash_v1               48.6
2048  1   fused_qkv_epilogue     79.4
```
So the epilogue-fused version regresses ~60% at seq=2048.

jorge: That gap screams epilogue kernel hot path. NVTX/nsys usually shows the epilogue taking most GPU time in these cases. Could be memory movement or divergence introduced by fusion. Try this quick profile incantation: 
```
nsys profile --output=prof.nsys --sample=none --trace=cuda,osrt ./run_attention_bench --model=gpt2xl --seq=2048 --bsz=1 --kernel=fused_qkv_epilogue
nsys stats prof.nsys | grep -i epilogue
```

alex: Pasted a few lines from the nsys output I captured: 
"fused_attn_epilogue_k (grid 256): 58.2ms, 73.9% GPU time"
"flash_attn_qkv_pack (grid 64): 3.2ms"
Also noticed `cudaMemcpyAsync` spikes around the same time window.

mei: Two hypotheses: (1) Our epilogue fusion adds conditional work per-thread (rope+bias+relu-like ops) that disables vectorized stores, causing many small stores and warp divergence. (2) For long sequences we hit the paged KV path and the allocator triggers device<->host memmoves; fused kernel's working set forces extra memcopies. Check memcopy call stacks in the timeline.

priya: If allocator/memcopy is involved that explains the sudden jump with seq. We should add a quick runtime fallback: if seq > 1024 and bsz <= 2, prefer flash_v1 variant (lower working set), otherwise enable fused. That would be a safe canary policy while we investigate. :thinking:

jorge: I prototyped a different approach: split the epilogue into two kernels — (A) bias+rope apply to Q/K/V tiles (vectorized), (B) the small reduce/permute epilogue. That reduces register pressure and seems to avoid the heavy memcopies. Locally it moves 79.4ms -> ~52ms for seq=2048. Not perfect but much better. Draft PR here: https://github.com/redwood/prs/498 (draft).

alex: Nice. Action items I want on the short list: 
1) Add the fallback rule in kernel_selector (canary config flag).
2) Add nsys wrapper to nightly regression job and grep for epilogue/memcpy counts.
3) Instrument KV allocator to emit memmove counts to telemetry so we can correlate regressions.

perf-bot: nightly benchmark run queued — run_id: 2026-03-17_0001

mei: I'll own the kernel_selector change and add unit tests for the heuristic.

priya: I'll add KV memmove counters to telemetry and a small microbenchmark that asserts memmove <= threshold (per-model).

jorge: I'll finish the split-epilogue PR and add a microbenchmark comparison.

alex: I'll coordinate a canary rollout after those three items land, and run the nsys traces on the canary machines. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
